title: Battle of Chausa
subtitle: Humayun is defeated by Sher Shah, reversing early Mughal gains in the east.
summary: At Chausa on 26 June 1539, Sher Shah defeated Humayun in a decisive battle. The defeat weakened early Mughal momentum and elevated Afghan power in the eastern subcontinent, with direct consequences for Bengal's political trajectory.
heroTagline: Chausa reversed the balance of power and delayed Mughal consolidation in Bengal's orbit.
whyItMatters: This event matters because it explains why the first Mughal intervention in Bengal did not immediately turn into stable control.
longTermLegacy: The Chausa defeat prolonged Afghan leverage in the east and postponed a durable Mughal settlement in Bengal.
identityMemoryNotes: Chausa remains a marker of how battlefield reversals in the Gangetic east shaped Bengal's long transition before full Mughal incorporation.
